newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-SOUTH KOREANS WERE IRRESPONSIBLE, ADMITS TEAM MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-SOUTH KOREANS WERE IRRESPONSIBLE, ADMITS TEAM MANAGER.

text.p: South Korean team manager, Kwon Seung-taik apologised on Thursday for the "irresponsible" behaviour of four of his top players in a world championship match which lasted just eight minutes.

In a second round mixed doubles tie on Wednesday, Kim Dong-moon and Ra Kyung-min, unseeded despite winning gold and silver at last year's Olympics, defeated the number eight seeds Ha Tae-kwon and Kim Shin-young 15-1 15-1.
Championship referee Torsten Berg has filed a report which will be brought before the full council of the International Badminton Federation on Saturday.

"It is regretful that this serious matter arose in the second round match," said Kwon. "We recognise the referee could decide that the match was not within the spirit of the competition, and we acknowledge that some spectators may think there was prior arrangement as to who should win.
"But while we accept the players behaved irresponsibly, we stress that it is not within the coaching staff's principles to press any player to artificially win or lose a game.
"We would attribute the result to long-term friendships among the players involved, and, perhaps, the fact that Ha Tae-kwon realises that his best medal chance is in the men's doubles."

Kim, gold medallist at Atlanta with a different partner, and silver medallist Ra had been forced to play in the qualifying rounds because as a new partnership they have no world-ranking despite their status in the sport.
With three South Korean pairs in the main draw, Kwon suggested that Kim and Ra should have been kept apart from their compatriots until the later stages.
"We are submitting an official request to the IBF Council that they consider separating players from the same countries in the draw," he said.
"We also apologise for any trouble caused by the Korean players and recognise the seriousness of the circumstances."
